info.desc: Suede is the debut album by English alternative rock band Suede, released in 1993 on Nude Records. At the time the fastest-selling debut album in British history, Suede debuted at the top of the UK Album Chart, won the 1993 Mercury Music Prize, and is often credited with starting the Britpop movement. The sound of the album has been compared to The Smiths and the early David Bowie era. .

podcast.title: Debut Album
podcast.body: Released in 1993 on the independent Nude Records label, this album was a pivotal release for the 1990s in the United Kingdom, completely revolutionizing the British recording market. Ed Buller, who was "the fashionable man" in the British music industry at the time, produced this album. "en 1993 salía uno de los discos más importantes para los 90 dentro del Reino Unido, que sería el disco de Suite, cuando sucede a que va a su primer disco revolucionaba totalmente el mercado discográfico británico."

podcast.title: Debut Album
podcast.body: Released in March 1993, this album immediately "collapsed" the United Kingdom music scene, entering the charts directly at number 1 and appearing on the covers of all UK music magazines. It achieved massive success across Europe and the United States with incredible sales, and due to a significant "hunger for musical novelties" in the UK, many music writers consider it one of the most important releases in British history. Unlike Blur's debut, Suede's first album garnered immense critical acclaim, solidifying their reputation as "the darling of British critics in 1993." It also won the Mercury Prize that year. The album's release was preceded by a historic cover on SELECT magazine in April 1993, which some texts claim officially marked the beginning of Britpop. "colapsa al reino unido."
